threads.body: Importing `dspy` at module import time makes the instrumentation package fail to import when `dspy` isn’t installed (a common/expected setup for optional instrumentations). To keep imports lazy, remove the top-level `import dspy` and instead import `dspy` inside `patch_dspy()` / `unpatch_dspy()` and (since `_start_retrieval_invocation` reads `dspy.settings`) either import `dspy` inside `_start_retrieval_invocation` or pass the configured RM/settings through from the patch site.

threads.body: Parsing with `json.loads(str(docs_attr))` can mask type regressions (e.g., if the attribute accidentally becomes a Python list/dict and `str(...)` produces non-JSON). Prefer asserting the attribute type is a JSON string (or bytes) and then calling `json.loads(docs_attr)` (decoding bytes if needed). This makes the test fail loudly if the span attribute is emitted in an unexpected type/format.

threads.body:
These branches are unreachable. [`Retrieve.forward`](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/dspy/retrievers/retrieve.py#L63-L65) flattens RM passages to strings before returning:

```python
passages = [psg.long_text for psg in passages]
return Prediction(passages=passages)
```

The wrapper only ever receives `Prediction` with `list[str]`. The `Mapping`, `id`, and `score` branches never run.

RMs that carry IDs or scores (like [`DatabricksRM`](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/dspy/retrievers/databricks_rm.py#L207)) override `forward()`, so patching `dspy.Retrieve.forward` does not intercept them anyway.

threads.body:
DSPy RM classes do not define `provider` or `provider_name` attributes (e.g. [`WeaviateRM`](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/dspy/retrievers/weaviate_rm.py#L52) uses `_weaviate_collection_name`, [`DatabricksRM`](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/dspy/retrievers/databricks_rm.py#L143) uses `databricks_index_name`). Probing them only works on the synthetic `_DummyRM` in tests and returns `None` in real DSPy usage.

Per the [semantic conventions for retrievals](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md#retrievals), `gen_ai.provider.name` is not required. Leave it unset unless mapping from known RM types.

threads.body:
[`dspy.Retrieve`](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/main/dspy/retrievers/retrieve.py#L43-L65) does not define `aforward` - it only has `__call__` and `forward`.

Because of this:
- The `_retrieve_aforward` wrapper and unwrap are dead code.
- `test_async_retrieve_execution` skips on real DSPy installs.
- The other two async tests only pass because they monkeypatch their own `aforward` onto the class.

Drop the async path until DSPy adds native async support for `Retrieve`.
